methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Memory Tricks for Irregular Verbs
content: Problem: Học sinh thường có xu hướng thêm "-ed" vào tất cả các động từ trong quá khứ (ví dụ: go -> goed, fly -> flyed).

teacher_contents.reading_passage: Last summer, Max went on a magic trip! He went to the beach with his family. They flew on a big airplane. "The airplane flew high in the sky!" said Max. At the beach, Max ran on the sand. He ran into the cold water. His sister came with a ball. "Come and play with me!" she said. They ran and played all day. At night, a colorful bird flew across the sky. The bird came from the green forest. Finally, they went back home. Max was tired but happy. "That was a great adventure!" he said.

listening_script.speed_note: Normal speed (130 wpm) — pause after each sentence for dictation section
listening_script.text: Last summer, Max went on a magic trip to the beach. His family flew on a big airplane. At the beach, Max ran on the sand and ran into the cold water. His sister came with a ball and they played all day. A colorful bird flew across the sky. It came from the green forest. Finally, they went back home. Max was tired but very happy.

teacher_contents.grammar_notes:
• Irregular verbs in past tense: go→went, come→came, run→ran, fly→flew
• These 4 verbs are the WEEK 29 target — students must produce them actively
• Key contrast: regular verbs add -ed (played, walked) / irregular verbs change form completely
• Avoid drilling as a list — keep in story context: 'Max WENT to the beach. The airplane FLEW high.'
• Spiral link: students learned was/were (W19-27) — now adding movement irregular verbs
teacher_contents.speaking_notes:
SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance (do NOT share with students):

Student A: Names one thing Max did at the beach (e.g., "Max ran on the sand").
Student B: Responds with what happened next using a sequence word (e.g., "Then, he ran into the water").
Goal: Use irregular verbs in past tense, chained with sequence words.

PULL-OUT TASK (S1):
— Show a picture of a beach/airplane. Ask: "What did Max do first?"
— Scaffold weak students: provide sentence frame "Max ___ to the beach. He ___ on the sand."
— Target elicitation: went / flew / ran / came

COMMUNICATIVE TASK TIP:
— If students say 'goed' or 'runned', model the correct form immediately: "We say 'went' — Max WENT to the beach."
— Stronger students: challenge them to use 3 irregular verbs in one story sentence.
teacher_contents.stem_extension:
STEM Link — Transportation & Speed (Geography/Science):
An airplane travels at ~800 km/h; a car at ~100 km/h; a person running at ~10 km/h. Ask students: 'Max flew to the beach on an airplane. If the beach is 800 km away, how long did the flight take?' (Answer: 1 hour.) Connect: 'Why do people choose airplanes for long trips?'
teacher_contents.in_class_speaking: Trip Story Chain (Pairs): Student A says the first event using 'went' (e.g., 'Last summer, I went to the beach.'). Student B continues with 'then' + a new verb (e.g., 'Then, I ran into the water.'). Continue alternating — each student must use a different irregular verb. Goal: produce a 4-event chain using went/came/ran/flew.
teacher_contents.vc_answer_key: beach, airplane, sand, cold, sister, bird, forest, home, tired, adventure

teacher_contents.reading_passage: Luna went on a trip to the mountain. First, she packed her bags. Then, her family went in a fast car. They didn't fly on an airplane. When they arrived, Luna ran up the rocky path. She ran very fast! A friendly cat came to say hello. "Hello, little cat!" said Luna. Suddenly, a big eagle flew over their heads! It flew very high in the clouds. After that, they went down the mountain safely. "The trip was amazing!" said Luna. "I want to go again next year."

listening_script.speed_note: Slightly slower (120 wpm) — this session focuses on matching task format
listening_script.text: Luna went on a trip to the mountain with her family. They went in a fast car, not an airplane. When they arrived, Luna ran up the rocky path very fast. A friendly cat came to say hello to Luna. Then, a big eagle flew over their heads. It flew very high in the clouds. After that, they went down the mountain safely. Luna said the trip was amazing.
listening_script.dictation: A big eagle flew over their heads and flew very high in the clouds.

teacher_contents.grammar_notes:
• Review: went / ran / came / flew — same 4 verbs, different story context
• New usage: negative past — 'They didn't fly on an airplane.' (did + not + base form)
• Sequence words review: First / Then / When / Suddenly / After that
• 'Arrived' is regular (arrive→arrived) — contrast with irregular verbs
• Key pattern: 'Luna RAN up the path' (direction) vs 'The eagle FLEW over their heads' (direction)
teacher_contents.speaking_notes:
SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance:

Student A: States one action Luna did (e.g., "Luna ran up the rocky path").
Student B: Continues with what happened next (e.g., "Then, a cat came to say hello").
Goal: 2-event chain using sequence words + irregular verbs.

PULL-OUT TASK (S2):
— Ask: 'How did Luna's family travel? Did they fly?' → elicit: 'No, they went in a car.'
— Scaffold: sentence frame 'They didn't ___. They ___.'  
— Target: distinguish 'flew' vs 'went (by car)' — two different travel verbs

DIFFERENTIATION:
— Weaker students: provide verb bank (went / ran / came / flew) for Speaking Checkpoint
— Stronger students: use 'Suddenly' and 'After that' as mandatory connectors
teacher_contents.stem_extension:
STEM Link — Geography & Elevation:
Mountains are higher in elevation than beaches. The Dead Sea is 430m below sea level (lowest point on Earth); Mount Everest is 8,849m above sea level (highest). Ask: 'Luna ran UP the mountain — why does your body feel more tired going uphill?' Connect to energy, gravity, and effort. 'Eagles fly HIGH — what body features help them stay up?' (large wingspan, hollow bones).
teacher_contents.in_class_speaking: Compare & Contrast Talk (Pairs): One student describes Max's beach trip (S1), the other describes Luna's mountain trip (S2). They must use at least 3 irregular verbs each and include one similarity and one difference. Example opener: 'Max went to the beach. Luna went to the mountain. Both went on trips!' Wrap up: whole class votes — beach trip or mountain trip?

teacher_contents.reading_passage: Tom went on a trip to the green forest. He wanted to see how animals move. First, a small rabbit ran out of the bushes. It ran very fast! Then, a beautiful butterfly flew in the air. It flew from flower to flower. Next, Tom went near the river. A little turtle came out of the water. It came very slowly. Finally, Tom ran back to his family. "Animals move in different ways!" he said. "Some animals fly, some animals run, and some come slowly!"

listening_script.speed_note: Normal speed (130 wpm) — Cambridge Flyers Listening Part 1 (multiple choice format)
listening_script.text: Tom went to the green forest to see how animals move. First, a small rabbit ran out of the bushes very fast. Then, a beautiful butterfly flew from flower to flower in the air. Next, Tom went near the river. A little turtle came out of the water very slowly. Finally, Tom ran back to his family. He said: 'Animals move in different ways — some fly, some run, and some come slowly!'

teacher_contents.grammar_notes:
• Mastery session: all 4 irregular verbs used in one story — went / ran / flew / came
• 'Some animals fly, some run, some come slowly' — present tense for general facts vs past tense for story events
• Error prevention: butterfly 'FLEW' (not 'flied'); turtle 'CAME' (not 'comed')
• Synthesis: students can now categorize: 'ran → movement on land; flew → movement in air; came → arrival direction'
• Portfolio target: write a complete paragraph using went + ONE other irregular verb
teacher_contents.speaking_notes:
SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance:

Student A: Names one animal from the story and says how it moves (e.g., 'The rabbit ran fast').
Student B: Names a different animal and says how it moves (e.g., 'The butterfly flew slowly').
Goal: Use ALL FOUR irregular verbs across the pair — went / came / ran / flew.

PULL-OUT TASK (S3 — Communicative Task):
— Ask: 'Can you tell me about ALL the animals Tom saw? Use past tense.'

STEM Link — Animal Locomotion (Science):
Animals move in 3 main ways: flying (birds, insects — use wings), running (mammals, reptiles — use legs), swimming (fish, turtles — use fins/flippers). Ask: 'The butterfly FLEW and the turtle CAME out of water — which moves faster? Why?' Science extension: 'What body part helps a butterfly fly?' (wings) vs 'What body part helps a turtle move in water?' (flippers). Connect math: if a rabbit runs at 50 km/h and a turtle walks at 0.3 km/h, how many times faster is the rabbit?
teacher_contents.in_class_speaking: Animal Movement Story Circle (Group of 3): Each student picks one animal (rabbit/butterfly/turtle). Student 1: 'I am the rabbit. I ran out of the bushes.' Student 2: 'I am the butterfly. I flew from flower to flower.' Student 3: 'I am the turtle. I came out of the water slowly.' Then all three say the moral together: 'Animals move in different ways!' Repeat with new animals invented by students.
